content-provenance.capability: Immutable creation provenance for Civweave artifacts and additive human-validation history
rules: Every result produced through Civweave AI generation is labeled ai-generated in generation metadata at creation time.
Structured generated objects also carry metadata.civweaveProvenance so persistence of outputJson preserves origin.
Persisted artifacts copy generation provenance into metadata.civweaveProvenance rather than attempting later AI detection.
Once an artifact has explicit ai-generated, human-authored, or deterministic-generated origin, later review may not rewrite that origin.
Human validation is additive metadata and never converts an AI-generated artifact into a human-authored artifact.
Legacy or imported content without reliable provenance is marked unknown and is never silently inferred to be human-authored.

passport-identity.capability: Local-first Civweave Passport creation and shared Passport identity continuity
rules: Passport creation is local-first and requires no AI, network service, Guild membership, or Anarchadia UI.
If an Anarchadia Passport already exists, every operating mode reuses that Passport ID and preserves its existing local state.
If no Passport exists, the owner initializes the same Anarchadia-compatible Passport state used by the existing Passport surface so Lud and Standard mode do not fork identity.
Presentation surfaces may display the Passport ID but may not mint a second Passport identifier or maintain a mode-specific Passport store.

operating-mode.capability: Cross-system Standard and Lud operating-mode policy
rules: Lud Mode does not invoke, load on demand, advertise, or require AI generation capabilities.
Lud Mode content discovery is provenance-based and admits only explicitly human-authored content; unknown and AI-generated content fail closed.
Human validation of AI-generated content does not make that content visible in Lud Mode because validation does not change creation origin.
Lud Mode creates or reuses the same local Passport identity as Standard Civweave and Anarchadia; it never maintains a Lud-only Passport.
Lud Mode exposes the canonical Guild login and membership surfaces, and joining a Guild does not enable AI while Lud Mode remains active.
Lud human creation delegates Quests to the canonical Cerbanimo quest engine and task/module additions to the canonical human proposal gate instead of maintaining parallel state owners.
The Lud-only manual record store is limited to human drafts or manifests that do not already have a canonical creation owner.
A Lud-funded human validation request consumes exactly 30 neurons from that resident's current-day included allowance and uses exactly two or three independent human validators.
Two-validator requests pay 15 neurons to each accepted validator; three-validator requests pay 10 neurons to each accepted validator.
Unused daily Lud validation capacity expires at the ordinary daily included-neuron reset and never becomes a rollover wallet balance.
Accepted validators receive a same-day neuron bonus that expires at the ordinary daily reset; it never rolls over or becomes a persistent or cash-backed lifetime compute balance.
The Lud download is an allowlisted package boundary, not a renamed copy of the ordinary offline campus.
The Lud download surface and packaged Lud campus contain no generated visual assets, images, logos, SVG illustrations, canvases, or background-image URLs.

settings.capability: Cross-system Settings entry, presentation, credential state, and fixed section layout
rules: One DOM Settings input owner per document.
The Settings input owner, presentation owner, and credential owner are the same module.
The canonical menu declares AI route, S.A.F.E., language, and downloaded-local-AI sections before it becomes visible.
Lazy services may populate a predeclared Settings section but may not insert a second Settings panel, dialog, launcher listener, or presentation root.
Legacy Settings modules are compatibility facades only and may not create DOM, attach document Settings click listeners, or publish themselves as authority.
Realm pages may style the shared control but may not create a second Settings implementation or listener.
Living School uses the family-shell Settings control and has no realm-local Settings button.
Browser prototypes, DOM prototypes, and Settings API methods may not be monkey-patched to repair Settings behavior.
Credential helpers may expose explicit compatibility methods but may not intercept Settings input, patch Settings open(), or mutate credential state at module load.
Realm stability/recovery layers may call the canonical Settings API programmatically but may not intercept Settings controls or carry dormant fallback listeners.

family-navigation.capability: Five-system navigation and expressive realm-status chrome
rules: The themed system navigation is the only module allowed to create five-system navigation DOM.
The family shell may own realm header, status, chat, and Settings chrome but may not create a second five-system navigation surface.
The retired #cwf104-tray and [data-cwf-system] family-navigation DOM contract must remain absent from active source.
Every first-class installed route receives the navigation owner through the install boundary.
No hidden, fallback, or compatibility family-navigation owner is permitted.

guide-chat.capability: Five private guide threads on one current conversation surface

local-ai-inference.rule: Settings may manage downloaded models but must never start inference on open.

guild-quest-publication.capability: Explicit member submission and shared Guild viewing of saved Weaveling Quests
rules: Any currently authenticated member may explicitly submit a saved Weaveling weave-plan to their own Guild.
The Guild authority assigns the publishing member, destination, publication identifier, and revision; client identity fields never grant authority.
Only the publishing member may revise or withdraw a publication, and stale revisions fail visibly.
Shared Quest records contain an allowlisted snapshot, never original conversation, private wish, evidence, profile, session token, or credential fields.
Local drafts remain device-owned and never become published merely because a Guild is selected.
The browser transport reuses host-node sessions and owns no parallel membership or publication store.
Both existing Guild deployment adapters execute the same portable publication domain contract.

host-node-access.capability: Device-bound Guild login, capacity sessions, membership admission, and neuron quota telemetry
rules: Only the owner writes browser Guild capacity sessions and device login credentials.
Capacity bearer tokens remain tab-scoped in sessionStorage; device login credentials remain local and are never dispatched in events.
Cloudflare AI generation and validation require a verified Guild capacity session in operating modes that permit AI.
Lud Mode may use the same Guild discovery, admission, membership, and session owner while its operating-mode policy continues to prohibit AI generation.
Human-validation neuron funding and claims reuse the verified capacity session; their browser client may read but never write the session store.
Paid-expansion availability may be discovered, but a new paid-expansion resident is never admitted without active membership authority.

node-reconstruction-backup.capability: Encrypted whole-node reconstruction checkpoints, retention, and replica storage
rules: Source systems remain canonical owners and export only explicitly portable records.
ABBA is an exact reconstruction/addressing codec and never replaces cryptographic commitments or authenticated encryption.
API keys, session bearer tokens, browser-bound signing keys, private authority keys, recovery secrets, and refresh tokens are never portable backup payloads.
Restore verifies the complete checkpoint before returning records and never silently mutates a source system.
Federated replica transport must retain application-level signatures and CMLP key separation.

private-messaging.capability: Offline-first encrypted member private messaging with opportunistic mesh and hidden online relay transport
rules: The user-facing member identity is @username; the derived username_pm@civweave.cc address is transport-only and must never be presented as the member's email address.
Private message plaintext is encrypted on the sending device before mesh, Hub, Worker, R2, or hidden-mail relay transport sees it.
The same encrypted envelope and UUID travel over local mesh and online relay so duplicate paths converge locally.
Inbound internet SMTP to _pm transport identities is rejected before message storage.
Paid human-visible email uses a separate entitlement-gated account and claim path.
Realm pages may call or present the canonical PM API but may not create realm-local messaging stores, encryption owners, relay protocols, or username registries.

radio.capability: Shared radio station and track suggestions

review.capability: Shared review surface and review handoffs
presentationRules: Capability owners supply corroborated persisted receipt IDs and scoped outcomes; the helper never accepts work or grants rewards.
Replay, Stop, map focus, and refresh do not invoke AI, publish, vote, transfer, or change review state.
Canonical reward append events animate only a new persisted eligible grant for the current account; bootstrap, duplicates, migrations, and failed writes remain silent.
An installed child delegates reward presentation only to its exact same-origin persistent parent; no duplicate child toast.
Finite motion, reduced-motion support, Lud text presentation, and stable same-receipt DOM survive redraws.

survival-assessment.capability: Offline first safety prioritization from user-reported conditions and locally stored references
rules: Cross-realm capability, not an additional chat system or realm.
No image bytes are persisted, uploaded, analyzed, or claimed as identification in v1.
Unknown is never safe; use only user-reported concerns and supplies.
Life-threatening hazards override repair, foraging, and research.
Never authorize edibility from a photograph or local source excerpt.
Show offline source provenance and errors without inventing verification.
Basic guidance requires no Guild, paid compute, model, or network.

starling-collective.capability: Bounded visible Collective planning and explicitly confirmed Guild proposals
rules: One user-started sequential planning batch with visible public role contributions and no always-on inference.
At most three reserved, proposed, blocked or published AI Quest lines per device and shared Guild.
At most six new lines per rolling 24 hours; failure, cancellation and abandonment do not refund history.
Model dialogue never completes work, votes, grants roles, activates a Quest or posts to a Guild.
Shared posting requires the exact saved proposal revision, hash and explicit human confirmation.
Passport claims require consent and distinguish declared skills, authenticated residents and verified capability.
Mesh discovery and billing seats never grant Guildmaster authority.
Shared completion requires trusted canonical proof; local model claims cannot attest it.
Guild local worker opt-in permits bounded signed persona turns and assistance offers, not claims, completed Quest beats, Guild votes or hosted spending.
The worker and the existing Collective planning workbench share the browser Starling inference lock.
